item.title: Madang Government gives K500,000 to upgrade school
item.description: The Madang Provincial Government has given K500, 000 to Madang Technical College, towards the college's initial preparations on becoming a Polytechnical college in the near future. Mr Pariwa was at the college yesterday and presented a dummy cheque plus the remittance advice stating that the money has been deposited into the college's account.
item.content:encoded:
The Madang Provincial Government has given K500, 000 to Madang Technical College, towards the college's initial preparations on becoming a Polytechnical college in the near future.

Mr Pariwa was at the college yesterday and presented a dummy cheque plus the remittance advice stating that the money has been deposited into the college's account.

At hand, to receive the dummy cheque was Deputy Principal- Administration, Robert Turik, and members of the college's Governing Council, Henry Kambuka and Alex Paira, witnessed by staff and students.

Mr Pariwa made a commitment last year that he would return to school, and he did yesterday with the dummy cheque.

"I decided to come back and support this institute because Madang Technical College is a distinguished institution of higher technical learning in the province. If we are serious about building the nation, then Madang Technical College is an institute of nation-building, so we must invest in it.

"I am proud to say that Madang Technical College is my highest technical learning institution in the province. I must look around in the province to ensure we build the capacity of the institution to empower the learning environment build and instill skills into our youth population," Pariwa said.

He added that whilst a lot of students get into primary schools through to high and secondary schools, not a lot get into universities because of the system and the capacity to accommodate the entire students.

Once updagraded to a polytechnical college, the institute can introduce more technical courses than what it is already offering.

Governor Pariwa further emphasized that if we truly want to build this nation, we must invest in human resources.

Mr Pariwa reiterated that his commitment to education is a priority, adding work on uplifting the level of Madang Technical College into a Polytechnical college starts now.

"It cannot happen overnight, but it has to start somewhere, somehow and it has started now. We will upscale the level with or without the support of the National Government because I have had enough of talks," Governor Pariwa said.

Meanwhile, Deputy Principal, Administration, Robert Turik commended Governor Pariwa for his government's support to the college.

Mr Turik also took the opportunity to highlight a new concept that Madang Technical College has embarked on to help create pathways for students in vocational schools around the country.

The concept is called Downlinking and Uplinking.

Turik explained, "We have gone out to several vocational schools in the province and outside including a study centre in Manus and a vocational school on Rabaul. Next, we are going to Tari. The Downlinking concept is to create pathways for the students as per the government's policy on leaving no one behind."

"So the students that don't go through the formal way of education, we are creating that pathway for them in accordance with the Department of Higher Education's PNG National Qualification Framework, which includes 11 steps from level one certificate to masters and doctorate level. So we are giving the chance competitively.

"When we downlink with a FODE or vocational school, their students have the opportunity to come through us and go out to pursue their studies in universities."

He added that FODE and vocational colleges are no longer second opportunities.They provide the same privileges as universities.

Under Uplinking, the college is creating Memorandums of Understanding or relationships with universities and other stakeholders.

Currently, the college has created an MOU with Divine Word University to help the students achieve the three years National Qualification Framework.

The program assists the students progress from level 1 certificate to diploma, degree, masters and even doctorate.

A similar MOU was recently signed with Ramu NiCo.

Alex Paira, a member of the college's Governing Council applauded Mr Pariwa and his government for honouring the commitment.

He said, "Your commitment to Madang Tech is now becoming obvious that you are serious, unlike other MPs who made commitments but never came back. So we at Madang Tech, we just have to make sure we do our part."

Mr Paira urged the college to be accountable, stressing that K500, 000 is a lot of money.

item.title: KCH strengthens Governance capability through training
item.description: Kumul Consolidated Holdings (KCH) has completed its fourth Director Development Program, equipping 17 middle management personnel from State-Owned Enterprises (SOEs) with skills to strengthen governance and prepare for potential future board roles. KCH Managing Director Professor, David Kavanamur presented certificates to participants at the conclusion of the three-day program, held from 28 to 30
item.content:encoded:
Kumul Consolidated Holdings (KCH) has completed its fourth Director Development Program, equipping 17 middle management personnel from State-Owned Enterprises (SOEs) with skills to strengthen governance and prepare for potential future board roles.

KCH Managing Director Professor, David Kavanamur presented certificates to participants at the conclusion of the three-day program, held from 28 to 30 September 2026 at the Aviat Club in Port Moresby.

Delivered by the PNG Institute of Directors (PNGID), with support from the Asian Development Bank’s Pacific Private Sector Development Initiative (ADB-PSDI), the program brought together 10 men and seven women nominated by PNG Ports, PNG DataCo, MVIL, Air Niugini, Kumul Agriculture and PNG Power.

Professor Kavanamur said the participants formed part of a growing pool of prospective directors whose skills, experience and merit could contribute to SOE boards.

“You are here because your organisations see in you the judgement, integrity and potential to take on greater responsibility,” he said.

Established in 2021, the program was designed to strengthen governance capability and increase women’s representation on SOE boards. The first three cohorts trained 65 women, several of whom have since served as directors.

This year’s fourth cohort included male participants for the first time, extending the initiative to develop governance capability among SOE personnel.

The program covered directors’ duties, the respective roles of boards and management, strategy, financial oversight, risk, accountability and effective boardroom conduct.

Professor Kavanamur encouraged participants to apply their learning immediately in their current roles.

“Use these skills now, instead of waiting for a Board appointment. In your current roles, you can ask better questions, use resources responsibly, raise concerns early and make decisions with integrity,” he said.

He thanked PNGID and ADB-PSDI for their continued support and acknowledged the participating SOEs for enabling their staff to attend.

item.title: Dr. Waiye murder case adjourned to Monday
item.description: The seven suspects in the murder case of the late Dr. Robert Waiye have been remanded at the Barawagi Correctional Institution after their first court mention today. The suspects, who have been in custody at the Kundiawa Police Station cells since 17th September, appeared before Senior Provincial Magistrate Edward Kupo at the Kundiawa District Court at 1:00 PM today.
item.content:encoded:
The seven suspects in the murder case of the late Dr. Robert Waiye have been remanded at the Barawagi Correctional Institution after their first court mention today.

The suspects, who have been in custody at the Kundiawa Police Station cells since 17th September, appeared before Senior Provincial Magistrate Edward Kupo at the Kundiawa District Court at 1:00 PM today.

The accused are Emmanuel Wax, 32, Sandra (Emmanuel) Limbia, 30, Sogan Dilu, 32, Moses John, 25, Kailo Andy, 25, Benjamin Kuat, 25, and Polly (Boi) Kaman, 30.

Magistrate Kupo explained the police allegations to the accused and ordered that all seven be charged under one joint charge.

He directed the Criminal Investigation Division and the arresting officer to finalize all charges over the weekend and present the completed file before the court on Monday, 5th October 2026.

Magistrate Kupo further ruled that any application for bail is a matter for the National Court.

The court precinct was packed with Simbu Provincial Police Commander, Chief Superintendent Mazuc Rubiang, police personnel, relatives of the late Dr. Waiye, the legal team of the Simbu Provincial Health Authority, and members of the general public who turned up to witness the first mention.

All seven accused have been transferred from the Kundiawa Police cells and remanded in custody at Barawagi Correctional Institution pending their next court appearance.

item.title: West Sepik rolls out mass drug administration and immunization campaign
item.description: West Sepik has launched a province-wide mass drug administration and immunization campaign targeting neglected tropical diseases, with health authorities urging all citizens to participate. The West Sepik Provincial Health Authority [WSPHA] officially launched its Mass Drug Administration [MDA] on Neglected Tropical Diseases [NTD] and Intensified Routine Immunization [IRI] campaign in Vanimo today
item.content:encoded:
West Sepik has launched a province-wide mass drug administration and immunization campaign targeting neglected tropical diseases, with health authorities urging all citizens to participate.

The West Sepik Provincial Health Authority [WSPHA] officially launched its Mass Drug Administration [MDA] on Neglected Tropical Diseases [NTD] and Intensified Routine Immunization [IRI] campaign in Vanimo today.

The campaign will run from October to November 2026 and targets lymphatic filariasis, a mosquito-borne disease that causes elephantiasis and chronic swelling, along with other neglected tropical diseases including yaws, ulcers and scabies.

WSPHA Chief Executive Officer Stanley Masi said West Sepik is the fourth province in the country to roll out the program, after New Ireland, East New Britain and West New Britain.

Mr Masi said many people in the province have suffered from these diseases in silence, with cases often not reported at health facilities.

"For too long our people have suffered from these tropical diseases. This mass drug administration will be given to all citizens to help us eliminate these diseases. I urge all citizens to participate. Parents, this is your responsibility to ensure your children receive these doses and immunizations for their future health," Masi said.

The PHA acknowledged the support of the World Health Organization (WHO), Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA), National Department of Health and the National Government for funding the program.

Chief Advisor of the JICA Lymphatic Filariasis Project in PNG, Dr. Masato Yamauchi, assured residents the treatment is safe.

"The provinces that have successfully rolled out this treatment have reported many people are now free from these diseases. West Sepik can also achieve this," Dr Yamauchi said.

The campaign will be implemented from Monday, 5th October to November 2026, with all health centres to administer treatment across districts and LLGs.

CEO Masi told NBC News that funding remains a challenge, with no support yet from the Sandaun Provincial Administration and most District DDAs, except Nuku District which has assisted.

The Sandaun Provincial Administration, through Deputy Provincial Administrator Timothy Teklan, has however pledged its support for the rollout.

item.title: Miss Bird of Paradise pageant Northern province- set for November
item.description: Prominent young women in Northern Province are gearing up to host the first of its kind Miss Bird of Paradise Northern Province Pageant in November 2026. Deputy Chairlady of Miss MBOP Northern Province 2026, Ms Kewana Inurapa, said the quest is the first of its kind that will be hosted in the province.
item.content:encoded:
Prominent young women in Northern Province are gearing up to host the first of its kind Miss Bird of Paradise Northern Province Pageant in November 2026.

Deputy Chairlady of Miss MBOP Northern Province 2026, Ms Kewana Inurapa, said the quest is the first of its kind that will be hosted in the province.

Ms Inurapa said six (6) contestants have already been confirmed to participate.

The Organizing Committee of the MBOP Northern Province has started its awareness program to high and secondary schools, including TVET schools in the province.

Ms Inurapa pointed out that the school awareness program is to make known to school-aged women to participate in such upcoming pageants in the future.

"Pageants are events where young women and girls have the opportunity to showcase their beauty and not only that, but the event goes beyond by exposing talents, networking, scholarship programs and employment opportunities," she said.

The upcoming MBOP Northern Province Pageant will be staged in the first week of November 2026.

The six contestants are all university students who will each represent selected LLGs, including Tamata, Higaturu, Tufi, Popondetta Urban, and Kokoda LLG respectively.

Meanwhile, Ms Inurapa said the MBOP Northern Province will be hosting its major Gala Fundraising Dinner in Port Moresby to raise funds towards the event.

She called on Northern people living in Port Moresby to come along and support the fundraising drive.

Ms Inurapa also said the Patron for the MBOP Northern Province 2026 is Northern Governor, Hon. Gary Juffa.

item.title: Brugam secondary in remote Maprik graduates 508 students
item.description: Brugam Secondary school, a South Sea Evangelical Church (SSEC) institution in the remote Bumbita-Muhian Local Level Government area of Maprik District, has graduated 508 students. The school held its 21st Grade 10 and 15th Grade 12 graduation on 1st October under the theme “Shine Through Discipline”, with 230 Grade 10 and 278 Grade 12 students graduating.
item.content:encoded:
Brugam Secondary school, a South Sea Evangelical Church (SSEC) institution in the remote Bumbita-Muhian Local Level Government area of Maprik District, has graduated 508 students.

The school held its 21st Grade 10 and 15th Grade 12 graduation on 1st October under the theme “Shine Through Discipline”, with 230 Grade 10 and 278 Grade 12 students graduating.

Located about 30 kilometres west of Maprik town, Brugam Secondary serves students from different districts across East Sepik Province, reflecting the South Sea Evangelical Church's commitment to providing education to communities beyond its immediate location.

Presenting the school's report, Principal Aminson Kundun acknowledged the continued support from the Maprik District Development Authority, Ambunti-Dreikikier District Development Authority and the Office of East Sepik Governor Allan Bird.

Kundun said the support had contributed to the development of the school, which caters for students from across the province and not only Maprik District.

Reflecting on what makes Brugam students unique, Kundun highlighted their determination to pursue their goals despite challenges after completing secondary education.

“Not all students who graduate from Brugam Secondary find spaces in tertiary institutions, but one thing that makes them stand out from the rest is that they don’t give up. They always work hard, find another way around and achieve their dreams,” Kundun said.

East Sepik Governor Allan Bird, who attended the graduation, delivered the keynote address and encouraged the graduates to continue learning.

“I don’t want you to stop learning. I am happy with the words of your principal. Even if you don’t make it, your grades are not good, use every opportunity to learn,” Governor Bird said.

He reminded the graduates that education was important whether they pursued professional careers or returned to their communities to work on their land.

“Whether you want to become a doctor or pilot, or want to go back and look after your land in your community, in both cases you need to be educated,” he said.

Governor Bird also challenged the graduates to look beyond their villages and province, saying education could open opportunities around the world.

“Don’t just aim for the country. Aim for the world. Education gives you the ticket to see the world. Don’t limit yourself to your village, province and country. The world is out there,” he said.

Meanwhile, South Sea Evangelical Church Education Secretary and Brugam Secondary School Board of Governors Chairman Mack Yarbange acknowledged Governor Bird's presence, saying it added value to the graduation and recognition of the students.

item.title: PNG to host 9th Pacific Media Summit in 2028
item.description: Papua New Guinea is set to host the 9th Pacific Islands News Association (PINA) Media Summit in Port Moresby in 2028. The Media Council of PNG (MCPNG) and the National Broadcasting Corporation of Papua New Guinea (NBC PNG) have jointly put forward a bid to host the regional summit.
item.content:encoded:
Papua New Guinea is set to host the 9th Pacific Islands News Association (PINA) Media Summit in Port Moresby in 2028.

The Media Council of PNG (MCPNG) and the National Broadcasting Corporation of Papua New Guinea (NBC PNG) have jointly put forward a bid to host the regional summit.

Speaking at the 8th Pacific Media Summit in Fiji recently, President of the PNG Media Council and newly appointed PINA President Neville Choi said the bid comes at an important time for the country and the Pacific media industry.

Choi said PNG wants to use its experience in working with government and the media industry to contribute to discussions across the Pacific.

“We are ready to host. And we have a very, very tough act to follow. I think the Fiji Media Association has shown that this is the level and standard of a PINA summit that we want to be.”

President Choi added that PNG's media industry has strengthened its relationship with government over the past three to four years, while continuing to push for self-regulation.

There are also concerns about possible changes in government and leadership following PNG's next general election, expected in 2027.

Choi stressed that the Media industry in PNG wants to build on the progress already made before those political changes take place.

He said PNG's experience could also provide lessons for smaller Pacific countries dealing with similar challenges around media regulation, press freedom and government relations.

PNG's cultural diversity, with more than a thousand tribes, was also highlighted as one of the country's strengths in bringing different voices together.

The joint bid also comes as the Pacific media industry faces growing challenges from misinformation, technology and pressure on press freedom.

Choi representing PNG acknowledged the high standard set by Fiji in hosting the 8th PINA summit, but said PNG is ready for the challenge.

“It’s going to be, like I said, a tough act to follow, but we are up to the challenge. And if you are all supportive, then we want you along with us on this," Choi said.

The Chief Executive Officer of the Solomon Islands Broadcasting Corporation (SIBC) Johnson Honimae seconded MCPNG AND NBC PNG's bid and move the motion in favour of PNG to host the 2028 9th PINA Media Summit in Port Moresby, PNG.

"This AGM, I want to support and move the bid from PNG Media Council and NBC PNG to host the 2028 PINA Summit".

item.title: Planning Secretary Konny Samuel ends 27-year public service career
item.description: Planning Secretary Koney Samuel has stepped down from office after 27 years of service to the Government and people of Papua New Guinea. Mr Samuel, 51, served as Secretary for the Department of National Planning and Monitoring for eight years.
item.content:encoded:
Planning Secretary Koney Samuel has stepped down from office after 27 years of service to the Government and people of Papua New Guinea.

Mr Samuel, 51, served as Secretary for the Department of National Planning and Monitoring for eight years.

He became Acting Secretary in July 2018 and was later appointed Secretary in May 2019. He served two consecutive terms before stepping down in October 2026.

Mr Samuel said he was leaving for personal reasons and believed it was time to give younger leaders an opportunity to serve.

“My decision to leave office stems from personal reasons. When I first took office as Secretary 2018, I was ready to take on the challenges of my new role, and I am proud of what we have achieved together over the years,” Mr Samuel said.

During his time as Secretary, Mr Samuel helped lead important national planning and development work.

This included seven Capital Investment Budgets, the Medium Term Development Plans III and IV, improvements to public investment management, PNG’s Second Voluntary National Review on the Sustainable Development Goals, and stronger partnerships with development partners.

He also supported reforms in infrastructure and the Water, Sanitation and Hygiene sector.

Mr Samuel thanked the Planning Ministers he worked with, including Richard Maru, the late Sam Basil, Renbo Paita and current Minister Sir Ano Pala.

He also thanked public servants, development partners, stakeholders and his family for their support.

“I believe the time is right for me to step aside and give opportunity to the younger generation of leaders to rise and take charge. I have served my country and people to the best of my ability, and I leave office with gratitude for the opportunity I have been given to serve,” Mr Samuel said.

He also thanked the Marape-Rosso Government for giving him the opportunity to serve as Secretary and thanked God for his strength and guidance during his 27 years of public service.

Meanwhile, the National Executive Council met on September 30 and appointed DNPM Deputy Secretary for Programming and Monitoring, Roger Kara, as Acting Secretary for the department.
